Tracking systems monitor two things at once: how fieldwork is progressing
overall, and what happened to each individual respondent. Together they prevent
sample loss, minimize attrition, and protect the representativeness of your
data---especially in panel studies that return to the same respondents over
multiple rounds.

## What You Will Find Here

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Foundations

- [Why Tracking Matters](why-tracking.qmd) - How tracking systems prevent sample
  loss, minimize attrition, and ensure representative data
- [Survey Tracking](survey-tracking.qmd) - Monitoring aggregate fieldwork
  progress with standardized metrics and real-time reporting
- [Respondent Tracking](respondent-tracking.qmd) - Outcome codes, contact
  information, tracking documentation, and attrition management for individual
  respondents
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Advanced Topics

- [Longitudinal Tracking Strategies](longitudinal-tracking.qmd) - Proactive
  techniques for maintaining contact across survey rounds in panel studies
- [Replacement Procedures](replacements.qmd) - When replacement is permitted at
  baseline, protocols to minimize selection bias, and why follow-up rounds never
  allow replacements
- [Mop-Up Operations](mop-up.qmd) - Reaching difficult respondents to achieve
  target response rates and minimize differential attrition
:::

## Getting Started

**Setting up tracking for a new study?** Read [Why Tracking
Matters](why-tracking.qmd) first, then set up [Survey
Tracking](survey-tracking.qmd) for progress monitoring and [Respondent
Tracking](respondent-tracking.qmd) for case management. Panel studies should
also review [Longitudinal Tracking Strategies](longitudinal-tracking.qmd).
